entities.summary:
The Battle of Velbazhd was a pivotal medieval conflict fought between the Bulgarian Empire and the Kingdom of Serbia on 28 July 1330, near the town of Velbazhd. This battle marked a significant turning point in the medieval politics of the Balkans, with the Bulgarian Empire emerging victorious.

The core events of the battle involved the Bulgarian forces led by Tsar Ivan Alexander, who clashed with the Serbian army under the command of Tsar Stefan Dušan. The battle resulted in the death of Tsar Stefan Dušan, which had a profound impact on the future of the Kingdom of Serbia.

The legacy of the Battle of Velbazhd can be seen in the subsequent decline of the Kingdom of Serbia and the rise of the Serbian Despotate. The battle also had a lasting impact on the medieval politics of the Balkans, shaping the relationships between the Bulgarian Empire and the surrounding kingdoms.

As the medieval historian John VI Kantakouzenos wrote, 'The defeat of the Serbs at Velbazhd was a calamity that shook the foundations of the Serbian kingdom.'
